questions.q: What did the twelve young men of Yathrib ask of the Prophet SAW after the first pledge of Aqabah?
options: A teacher who would teach the Quran and lead prayer
questions.explain: The two most basic things: the Quran and prayer.

questions.q: Who came to drive Mus'ab away but believed after hearing the Quran?
questions.explain: They believed after hearing the Quran.

questions.q: What are the right qualities of a caller to Islam according to the ustaz?
options: Command of the Quran, interpersonal skill, character and wisdom, not just a degree
questions.explain: Choose a caller with the right qualities.

questions.q: Why did the Prophet SAW send young Mus'ab together with the more senior Abdullah bin Umm Maktum?
options: To balance youthful zeal with senior maturity
Because they were the only ones available
questions.explain: Balance young enthusiasm with senior maturity.

questions.q: What did As'ad advise Mus'ab when a good opportunity opened?
What is the warning about love of popularity for a caller?
options: Guard yourself against love of popularity
questions.explain: A caller can easily feel people accepted Islam because of his skill.

questions.q: Mus'ab asked to be heard first and promised to leave if they disliked it.
questions.explain: True. Offer to be heard first with confidence.

questions.q: A caller may work casually without phases and planning.
questions.explain: False. Work systematically; Mus'ab and As'ad mapped out phases.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: As'ad gathers forty for Friday prayer
Twelve young men ask for a teacher

questions.explain: The request for a teacher, Mus'ab was sent, As'ad's house became the base, Usayd and Sa'd believed, then Friday prayer.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: One who teaches the Quran, Mus'ab's title
An open area near Madinah where Friday prayer was held

questions.explain: Al-Muqri is the Quran teacher, Naqi' al-Khadimat is the Friday site, fiqh aqalliyat is minority fiqh, and shuhrah is love of fame.
